It specifies pencil-and-paper administration with about 2 hours of testing per student and a total of about 7 hours of test items distributed across different student booklets, implying a planned complex sampling and booklet design typical of PISA. It also describes background questionnaires for students (20–30 minutes) and principals (30 minutes), but it does not provide any information about the use of complex survey weights (e.g., student/sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures. data.outcome_summary: This OECD/PISA framework describes how reading, mathematical, and scientific literacy are operationalized for the PISA 2000 cycle. It specifies pencil-and-paper administration with a total testing time of about 2 hours per student, while the overall item pool totals about 7 hours and is split across different booklets so that students receive different combinations of items. Each domain is organized into three dimensions (processes, knowledge/understanding, and context of application), and tasks use a mix of multiple-choice and constructed-response formats with marking guidance (including partial credit and two-digit marking for open items). The framework also outlines the assessment cycle (major domain emphasis: reading in 2000, mathematics in 2003, science in 2006) and the intended outputs: profiles of knowledge and skills, contextual indicators, and trend indicators for policy analysis. No empirical model estimation, PV computation, or ML-based prediction results are reported in this text.
